app.name: DeRechi
app.description: Lost and found notices for your city. Post in a minute, no account needed.

home.benefit1Text: Whoever responds leaves their contacts, and we pass them to the author of the notice by SMS or email.
home.benefit2Text: On a notice, the number is only partly visible and the email not at all. Only someone who responded gets the full number.
home.benefit3Text: One person can get an author's number at most once a week, so your contacts don't end up on spam lists.
home.benefit4Text: Notices go live at once. A moderator reviews them and removes what does not belong here.
home.benefit5Text: No account or password needed: a way to reach you is enough.
home.faqQ1: How do I contact the person who found it?
home.faqA1: Contacts on a notice are shown in part, to keep spam away. Press “It's mine, send my contacts” on the notice: we pass your phone and email to the finder by email and SMS, and they get back to you. The same works the other way round on a lost notice.
home.faqQ2: How can I be sure I'm returning it to the real owner?
home.faqA2: Don't show every detail in your notice. Ask the owner to describe what the photo doesn't show: what's in the wallet, which keyring is on the keys, what's on the phone's lock screen. Meet somewhere busy.
home.faqQ3: I found someone's documents. What should I do?
home.faqA3: Post a notice, but don't photograph pages with personal data or write the document number: the type of document and, if needed, the owner's name are enough. If the owner doesn't come forward, you can hand the documents to the police.
home.faqQ4: Can I keep what I found, or ask for a reward?
home.faqQ5: How do I find my thing in the list faster?
home.faqA5: Pick the category and the dates when you lost it: dates narrow the list the most. On the found side, turn on “Near me” to see things found within 10 km of you. Search in plain words: it looks through titles and descriptions.

safety.title: Safety
safety.metaDescription: How DeRechi protects your contacts and payments, and how to return a lost item safely.
safety.intro: DeRechi brings strangers together, so we make sure your contacts don't end up in the wrong hands, and we show you how to steer clear of scammers.

contacts.title: Contacts are not published
contacts.text: A notice shows its phone and email only in part. Only someone who responded to the notice and paid gets the full number, and nobody gets the email.

replies.title: Only the author sees your response
replies.text: The contacts you leave in a response go only to the notice's author, by email and SMS. They never appear anywhere on the site.

limit.title: Numbers can't be collected in bulk
limit.text: One person can get an author's number at most once a week, so your contacts don't end up on spam or scam-call lists.

accounts.title: No passwords to leak
accounts.text: DeRechi has no accounts, so there are no passwords to steal or guess.

moderation.title: Checks and moderation
moderation.text: Forms check that a person, not a bot, is sending them. A moderator removes notices that break the rules or expose someone else's data.

retention.title: Data isn't kept forever
retention.text: Contacts from responses are deleted after a year. Once the item is back, the notice goes to the archive and disappears from the site.

prepay.title: Don't pay until the item is in your hands
prepay.text: A scammer asks for money upfront “for delivery”, “for storage” or as a reward, then disappears. Pay only when you meet.

codes.title: You don't need codes to receive money
codes.text: A card or account number is enough to send you a reward. Anyone asking for an SMS code, CVV, PIN, or to “follow a link to receive the payment” wants to drain your card.

verify.title: Don't hand over or collect an item on trust
verify.text: Ask for a detail that isn't in the notice. And whoever really found your item can easily show a photo of it next to a note with today's date.

meet.title: Meet in public, not at home
meet.text: Don't share your home address or invite anyone over. Better in daytime, at a café, a shopping centre or outside a police station.

documents.title: Don't send photos of documents or cards
documents.text: They are used to take out loans and break into accounts. Hand a found card to the bank and documents to the police.

report.title: Spotted a scammer? Tell us
report.text: Send the link to the notice to {email} and we'll take it down. Keep the messages: you'll need them for a police report.

report.title: Start from the side you are on
report.text: Lost something, or picked something up? Both take a minute and neither needs an account.

search.title: Look before you post
search.text: Search by what you lost and roughly when. Whatever you set lands in the address bar, so the search can be bookmarked or sent to someone.

recent.title: The latest finds
recent.text: Things people picked up in the last few days. Open one to see the place, the date and how to reach the finder.

language.title: Five languages
language.text: Ukrainian, English, Polish, German and French. Your choice is remembered and carries over to the admin panel.

details.title: Describe the thing plainly
details.text: A short, ordinary name works best: scratches, wear and what was inside belong in the description.

photo.title: A photo does most of the work
photo.text: Drop the file here and it goes straight to our storage. A found item cannot be posted without one.

place.title: The last place you are sure about
place.text: Pick it from the suggestions so the coordinates come along with the name.

contacts.title: Who sees your contacts
contacts.text: Your contacts are shown only in part. Whoever recognises the item sends you theirs through the notice, and you get them by email and SMS.

game.prizeText: He gives up: you are officially his best friend. Nobody spots a lost thing faster than you.
